slides.say: A hall manager plans to set out the same number of chairs in each of eight rows. One row must be removed to make room for a stage. Each of the seven remaining rows must then hold three more chairs. How many chairs per row were originally planned?
They ask how many chairs per row were planned. So, as in the tip, let x be exactly that. We'll solve it three ways, the math way with an equation, with an insight, and by plugging in the answers.
Let's start with the math way, slowly. The plan was eight rows, with x chairs in each row. So the plan has eight x chairs.
at: So the plan has eight x

slides.say: In reality, one row was removed, so seven rows are left. And each row gets three more chairs, x plus three. So in reality there are seven times x plus three chairs.
Why can we write an equation? Because the number of chairs didn't change. They're the same chairs, just set out in fewer rows. So eight x is equal to seven times x plus three.

slides: This is worth remembering. When things only move around, the total stays the same. When some are removed, the total drops, and when some are added, it grows.

slides.say: Now we open the brackets. Seven times x is seven x. Seven times three is twenty-one. So eight x is seven x plus twenty-one. Take seven x from both sides, and x is twenty-one.
at: So eight x is seven x
Take seven x from both sides

slides.say: What is x? The number of chairs per row in the plan, exactly what they asked. Twenty-four, choice number one, is a trap. It's the new number per row, twenty-one plus three. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now the insight. We start again from the givens, and think about the chairs of the row that was removed. Those chairs didn't disappear. They were moved to the other rows.
Seven rows are left, and each one got three more chairs. Seven times three is twenty-one. So the removed row had twenty-one chairs.
And every row was planned with the same number of chairs. So every row had twenty-one chairs in the plan.
[pause] And we can also plug in the answers. We start again from the givens. A choice works if eight rows of it hold the same number of chairs as seven rows of three more.

Choice number one, twenty-four. Eight times twenty-four is a hundred ninety-two. Seven rows of twenty-seven are seven times twenty-seven. That's a hundred forty plus forty-nine, a hundred eighty-nine. Not the same, so it's out.
at: Not the same, so it's out

slides.say: Choice number two, twenty-one. Eight times twenty-one is a hundred sixty-eight. Seven rows of twenty-four are seven times twenty, a hundred forty, plus seven times four, twenty-eight. Together that's a hundred sixty-eight too. The same chairs, so it fits. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
